newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Rugby Union - Coffin to miss N.Transvaal game Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union - Coffin to miss N.Transvaal game Saturday.

text.p: WELLINGTON, March 13 - Wellington Hurricanes prop Phil Coffin narrowly escaped serious injury in last Friday's Super 12 match with the Canterbury Crusaders and will miss Sunday's match with Northern Transvaal in New Plymouth as a result, NZPA reports.

Treatment this week for a back injury has Coffin at about 80 percent fitness and he will either act as reserve or sit out altogether and allow Taranaki's Gordon Slater on to the bench. Wellington's Billy Cavubati will play at tighthead.
Coffin said today he was lucky to escape with as little damage as he did, after being caught awkwardly when the first scrum of the night at Lancaster Park came together with bad timing.
"Everyone came on to me late in the first scrum, I twisted and popped a couple of vertebrae. Luckily, though, they haven't been damaged. It could have been worse."
Coffin said he would be right for the team's trip to South Africa in a couple of weeks.
"I'm waiting for the swelling to come down at present, but I had a run yesterday and it didn't feel too bad. But we've decided to give it another week to come right."
Wellington flanker Filo Tiatia is another likely to have a rest. Tiatia has on-going knee and shoulder problems which would benefit from not playing this week, and the bye week next week.
Wellington team-mate Martin Leslie looks certain to play on the open side in partnership with Chresten Davis and Karl Williams.

Young lock Dion Waller is another likely to start. His aggression and ability to get around the field is handy, but his lineout ability against the big men from Northern Transvaal will rely very much on an improvement in timing.
Mike Russell could be the man to miss out.

Young Auckland loose forward Finau Maka has been drafted into the squad and will be a reserve on Sunday and also make the trip to South Africa until national sevens player Dallas Seymour returns from the World Cup in Hong Kong.

Likely Hurricanes team: Jarrod Cunningham, Alex Telea, Alama Ieremia, Tana Umaga, Jason O'Halloran, Steve Bachop, Jon Preston, Karl Williams, Martin Leslie, Dion Waller, Mark Cooksley, Chresten Davis, Bill Cavubati, Norm Hewitt, Mark Allen (captain).
